headline: Bangladesh Board Sets Tk 17,000 Garment Wage
deck: Four of six board members backed the new rate, while the workers’ representative said the outcome still fell short.
body: Dhaka Tribune reported that Bangladesh’s Minimum Wage Board fixed the ready-made-garment minimum monthly wage at Tk 17,000; bdnews24.com said the increase was Tk 4,500, and Al Jazeera reported a 36% pay rise. [E1] [E2] [E4]
bdnews24.com reported that four of the board’s six members voted for Tk 17,000 and the other two backed Tk 18,000. [E3]
The board has now named a wage after the paper’s Nov. 6 coverage recorded that it had not specified the size of the increase. [E6]
Babul Akhter, the labour representative on the wage board, told reporters: “Although we are not completely satisfied, the outcome is not entirely bad either.” [E5]

evidence_box.fragment: The Minimum Wage Board has fixed the minimum monthly wage for workers in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) industry at Tk17,000, up 36% from the existing Tk12,500, following several rounds of negotiations between factory owners and workers’ representatives.
